clue.text: Find fault with door's woodwork

parts.note: to carp is to find fault, to nag
a door is a way in

explanation.surface: Someone criticising the joinery on a door.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of door's is just the possessive of the surface; the door piece is followed directly by the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpentry is the craft of working timber, so woodwork is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Cheesy opponent in the classroom?

parts.note: the surface suggests a cheesy, corny rival; the setter means the thing always set against cheese in 'as different as ___ and cheese'
the same stuff a teacher writes on the blackboard with

explanation.walkthrough: Two things are said to be as different as this and cheese, so it is cheese's natural opposite; the classroom pins down the writing stick.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft white limestone stick used on blackboards is the traditional opposite of cheese in the English idiom.

clue.text: Enrol again to study at US university

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A student signing up once more to take a course in America.
explanation.definitionFit: To readmit is to let someone back in, as a college does when re-enrolling a former student.

clue.text: Joanna Blackwood?

parts.note: looks like a woman's first name; in rhyming slang a joanna is a piano
looks like a surname; read as two words it is the dark timber used for a piano's black keys

explanation.walkthrough: 'Joanna' is Cockney rhyming slang for piano (joanna/pianna). The dark keys on a piano were traditionally made of a black hardwood, which is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is the black tropical hardwood once used for a piano's sharps and flats, so it is literally the piano's black wood.

clue.text: Renegade's skill is to go about organising riot

indicators.note: going about means turning round, so the word is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

indicators.note: organising puts things into a new order, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rebel's talent lies in stirring up a riot.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade deserts their side, and a traitor is one who betrays their own cause; the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Duke's rent from God's own county!

parts.note: the Duke of York, with the possessive kept as a letter
to hire is to rent

explanation.surface: A tenant paying rent to a duke out of a proud northern county.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Duke's is not a link: it stays in, so the Duke gives his title plus the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkshire, the large English county in the north, is nicknamed God's own county by its proud inhabitants.

clue.text: Craze on One Direction's in decline

definitions.note: read as 'is in decline', a verb phrase matching the verb fade

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing on another simply follows it

parts.note: a fad is a passing craze
one compass direction: east

explanation.surface: The boy band One Direction is no longer the craze it was.
explanation.walkthrough: One Direction looks like the pop group, but it is just one point of the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: To fade is to dwindle or weaken gradually, which is what something in decline does.

clue.text: Fiat can design for enthusiast

indicators.note: to design something is to plan its layout afresh, so the letters are laid out anew

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The carmaker Fiat can produce designs aimed at car lovers.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanatic is an extremely keen devotee, so an enthusiast in a strong sense.

clue.text: A local fixture?

parts.note: read plainly: a match between nearby teams, a local derby on the sports calendar
a local is a British pub, and this fixture is a target fixed to its wall

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is the neighbourhood pub, and a fixture can be something screwed to the wall rather than a scheduled game.
explanation.definitionFit: The board for the pub game of darts hangs permanently on the wall of many British pubs.

clue.text: Dad managed alternatively logical and unjustified suspicion

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
to run a business is to manage it

indicators.note: alternately read as every other one, so only the even-placed letters of the next word are kept

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A father, being alternately rational and baselessly suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternatively' looks like it means 'or', but here it picks alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Paranoia is irrational distrust of others, a suspicion with no basis in fact.

clue.text: Was completely used to feeling lustful about Romeo

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps itself round the following letter

parts.note: randy is British slang for sexually eager
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone who grew accustomed to lusting after Shakespeare's Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was completely used to' reads as one idiom, but the definition stops at 'used'.
explanation.definitionFit: A supply that ran dry was exhausted, every last bit of it used up.

clue.text: Naughty thing's wearing blue that's very revealing!

indicators.note: someone wearing a colour is dressed in it, so the first word sits inside the clothing word

parts.note: sky blue; the sky is blue
an imp is a mischievous little creature

explanation.surface: A mischievous person in a very daring blue outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpy clothing uses little fabric and so shows a lot of skin.

clue.text: Examine underground lab equipment

parts.note: to test is to examine
the Tube is London's Underground railway

explanation.surface: Inspecting the gear in a laboratory below ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A test tube is a slim glass vessel, one of the basic items of laboratory apparatus.

clue.text: Unrestrained desire's nothing new

parts.note: a want is a desire
zero, shaped like O
standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Wild, unchecked longing is nothing novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanton describes behaviour without restraint, often reckless or lascivious.

clue.text: Mannerism designed to impress? No thanks, love!

indicators.note: saying no to something refuses it, so those letters are left out

parts.note: an affectation is a put-on manner meant to impress
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Refusing a showy gesture with a polite 'no thanks, darling'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' looks like a term of address ending the remark, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Affection is fond feeling or tenderness, a gentle form of love.

clue.text: Cuss rain that's knocked over sunflower

indicators.note: something knocked over is upset and jumbled, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
only the front part, sun, is used here: S is its standard abbreviation, as in Sun. for Sunday; the rest of the word is the definition

explanation.surface: Swearing at the rain that has flattened a sunflower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sunflower' reads as one word, but it splits: the first part supplies a letter and the rest is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissus is a genus of spring flowers that includes daffodils and jonquils.

clue.text: Mac cartoon loses nothing in translation, having excellent content

indicators.note: content is what is held inside, so this piece goes within the reworked letters
translating turns words into a different form, so the remaining letters are rearranged
a word that loses something has a piece taken away from it

parts.note: taken as written
zero, shaped like O; one of the two Os goes
A1 means first-rate; the 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A Mac cartoon that keeps its quality when translated into another language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mac' suggests Apple computers, but a mac is British for a waterproof coat (short for mackintosh).
explanation.definitionFit: A mac, short for mackintosh, is a rainproof overcoat, the same garment as the answer.

clue.text: Sure about route?

parts.note: of can mean about, as in 'speak of'
a course is a route taken

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether they are certain of the way.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Sure!' and 'Of course!' are both emphatic ways of saying yes, certainly.

clue.text: Busy working man's after time to take leave

indicators.note: after places the word before it immediately behind the word that follows

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
T is the standard abbreviation for time
he is the pronoun for a man
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: A hard-working man is due some time off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the go is constantly active, never resting, which is to say busy.

clue.text: Intending to marry with aim to secure good number of years

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the outer word holds the others within it

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose
G is the standard abbreviation for good
an age is a period of many years

explanation.surface: Someone planning a wedding with an eye to long-term security.
explanation.definitionFit: An engaged couple have formally agreed to marry, so they intend to wed.

clue.text: Old coin possibly does contain copper

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside, so the metal's symbol goes within the rearranged letters
possibly suggests one arrangement among many, so the letters may be reordered

parts.note: taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Wondering whether an antique coin is made partly of copper.
explanation.definitionFit: The escudo was the currency of Portugal before the euro, so it is an old coin no longer in use.

clue.text: Caught donkey very enthralled by acres of tropical food

indicators.note: someone enthralled by another is held captive, so this letter is gripped inside the next pair

parts.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
an ass is a donkey
a is short for acre, so acres plural gives two
v is the standard abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A donkey that has eaten a field of exotic crops.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassava is a starchy tropical root, the source of tapioca and a staple food in many hot countries.

clue.text: Very critical of scab briefly taking night shift

indicators.note: a word said briefly is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to shift things is to move them about, so the letters change places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Harsh words for a strike-breaker who takes on the night shift.
explanation.walkthrough: A scab is a worker who crosses a picket line; 'night shift' reads as a working rota, but shift is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Scathing remarks are bitterly severe, which is to say very critical.

clue.text: Hurts' cheerful performance gets small following

indicators.note: following means coming behind, so the last piece goes at the end

parts.note: feeling up is feeling cheerful
a set is a band's or comedian's performance
S is the standard abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: The band the Hurts put on a cheery show that draws a modest crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of Hurts' is surface dressing; the definition is the verb hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset someone is to hurt their feelings, so upsets matches hurts as a verb.

clue.text: Not in shape for fun run I finish fourth from last

indicators.note: finishing fourth in a race means coming in at fourth place, which fixes where this letter stands
colours that run spread out of place, so the word before is jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: taking from the last of something means only its end letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A runner who is out of condition comes fourth from the back in a charity race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fourth from last' reads as one placing, but it splits: I stands in fourth place, and the closing letter comes from the word last.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfit means in poor physical condition, out of shape.

clue.text: Small alteration to model's ineffectual

parts.note: the Ford Model T, the classic early car
weak means lacking force or effect

explanation.surface: A minor change to a design that does not work well.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweak is a slight adjustment made to fine-tune something.

clue.text: Whisks right on south, after taking M9 to Edinburgh, initially

indicators.note: after puts the first group behind the pieces named later in the clue

parts.note: M stays as written and 9 is IX in Roman numerals

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

parts.note: opening letter
R is the standard abbreviation for right
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Driving directions: go south and turn right after taking the M9 motorway to Edinburgh.
explanation.walkthrough: The M9 is a real Scottish motorway, which hides the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisks and mixers are both kitchen tools for beating or blending ingredients.

clue.text: Astounded by nonsense and laughed uproariously

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two pieces sit next to each other with the second named going first

parts.note: guff is informal for nonsense, empty talk
awed means filled with wonder

explanation.surface: Someone stunned by rubbish, then roaring with laughter at it.
explanation.definitionFit: To guffaw is to give a loud, hearty laugh, so the past tense is laughing uproariously.

clue.text: Found optical part that's loose

indicators.note: part signals that only a portion of the words before it is wanted

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Discovering that a component of a lens has come loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' reads as an adjective, but it is the verb meaning to untie or set free.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose a knot or fastening is to undo it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Distract from right path

parts.note: right is one side, as opposed to left
a track is a path

explanation.surface: Leading someone astray from the proper way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right path' reads as the straight and narrow, but right is a side and path is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidetrack someone is to divert their attention from the main point, to distract them.
